text.insert: One held experiment answers the platform unknowns this spec depends on, and a short list of integration questions remains open beside it. The experiment stays held with the image groundwork: it runs only after the harness working-tree changes are committed and the Linux objdiff build exists.
Uncompressed image size and per-sandbox disk headroom against the 10 GiB container cap, from the ~2.7 GiB bundle.
MWCC-under-wibo runtime behavior on the platform's runners; the static i686 wibo is golden-verified locally, leaving only the foreign-kernel risk.
Exec round-trip latency for chatty tool loops, versus the multi-second model turns that dominate.
Stop-to-start wake latency, which sets the stop-while-thinking idle threshold.

steps.text: Bake the image: run build_image_bundle.sh under MANIFEST.md authority with the two pending artifacts added
held until the harness changes land and the musl objdiff exists
One full round trip: create a sandbox, push a seed bundle, build one unit incrementally, score it, download the verdict, delete
time every step: create, upload, build, score, download, delete
Stop the sandbox, start it, and time to exec-readiness
Optional: the same experiment at epoch-boundary scale with a full report build

text.insert: Canonical tool paths in the worker packet are verified on the host and would misreport the sandbox; verification moves to the sandbox or trusts the image manifest.
Corpus tools that also read workspace files (m2c_decompile notably) need a per-tool ruling: run sandbox-side or fetch inputs first.
Platform snapshots deactivate after two weeks unused; the runbook needs a keepalive or reactivation step.
The epoch boundary's full report build is the one remaining host build; giving epochs their own larger sandbox is deferred until the worker path is proven.
Stale-lease refusal semantics (error surface, retry policy) are unspecified in the authority contract; the sandbox spec inherits whatever that contract decides rather than defining its own.
